name: SaaS subscriptions
story: RavenStack, a B2B SaaS startup selling AI team tools on Basic, Pro and Enterprise plans. Accounts, subscriptions, product usage, support and churn from 2023 to 2024. Fully synthetic.

columns.name: referral_source
columns.description: How the account found the product

columns.name: has_churned
columns.description: Account has churned at least once

tables.name: fct_subscriptions
tables.description: One row per subscription period. A plan change starts a new subscription row.

columns.name: mrr_amount
columns.description: Monthly recurring revenue in USD (0 for trials)

tables.name: fct_feature_usage
tables.description: One row per feature per subscription per day of use.
tables.grain: One row per feature per subscription per day of use

columns.name: satisfaction_score
columns.description: CSAT 1 to 5; null when not answered (41%)

tables.name: fct_churn_events
tables.description: One row per churn event. An account can churn, come back and churn again.

columns.name: reason_code
columns.description: budget, competitor, features, pricing, support, unknown

columns.name: is_reactivation
columns.description: The account had come back before this churn

columns.name: feedback_text
columns.description: Short exit feedback; null when not given

tests.test: churned accounts have no open subscription

metrics.name: mrr
metrics.description: MRR on a date: sum mrr_amount of paid subscriptions active that day (start_date <= d and (end_date is null or end_date > d)). Value shown is for 2024-12-31.
metrics.sql: SELECT SUM(mrr_amount) FROM saas.fct_subscriptions WHERE NOT is_trial AND start_date <= DATE '2024-12-31' AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date > DATE '2024-12-31')

metrics.name: active_accounts
metrics.description: Accounts with at least one active paid subscription on a date. Value shown is for 2024-12-31.
metrics.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) FROM saas.fct_subscriptions WHERE NOT is_trial AND start_date <= DATE '2024-12-31' AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date > DATE '2024-12-31')

metrics.name: arpa
metrics.description: Average MRR per active account = mrr / active_accounts on the same date.
metrics.sql: SELECT SUM(mrr_amount)/COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) FROM saas.fct_subscriptions WHERE NOT is_trial AND start_date <= DATE '2024-12-31' AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date > DATE '2024-12-31')

metrics.name: churn_events
metrics.description: Count of rows in fct_churn_events in a period. The churn source of truth (see caveats).
metrics.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM saas.fct_churn_events WHERE churn_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-01-01' AND DATE '2024-12-31'

metrics.name: csat
metrics.description: Average satisfaction_score of answered tickets (nulls excluded).

caveats: Fully synthetic data, generated to look like a real SaaS business.
A plan change creates a new subscription row; sum MRR over subscriptions active on a date, never across all rows.
Accounts can churn more than once (is_reactivation).
satisfaction_score is missing for 41% of tickets.
The three churn signals disagree: dim_accounts.has_churned, fct_subscriptions.is_churned and fct_churn_events. Use fct_churn_events for churn counts and say so.
A churn event does not close the account's subscriptions: most churned accounts still have open subscriptions, so 'active' overstates retained revenue.
Subscription starts grow steeply through 2024, so most rows are recent.
questions: What was MRR at the end of each month in 2024?
Which churn reasons lead to the biggest refunds?
Do accounts that hit more errors churn more? Test it.
Do our three churn flags agree? Which should we trust?
Which features do Enterprise accounts use most?
